challenge: Kill-rule 'referenceable live pilot' is satisfied by the first fractional go-live (customers_per_year/12 per month): A3 passes on 0.25 of a customer at month 22. Model error.
evidence: Scratch re-run requiring cumulative go-live >= 1 customer: A3 base paused at 24 ($846k at risk); B base paused at 24 ($1.24M); all A3 month-0/derived kill-sensitivity variants flip to paused. Contradicts 14 s6 'A3 passes under every cost-center definition tested'.
proposed_change: Count a pilot only when cumulative go-live of an Unbound (E2) sponsor stream >= 1; regenerate 14/16/19 and P3-CLM-MOD006.

challenge: A3 base passes the named-partner test only on a tie (named partner 6 = cost-center 0 + 6, strict '>'); base is the mode of triangular 3/6/12, whose median is ~6.8 and P(>6)=67%.
evidence: Re-run with named_partner base 7: A3 base paused at month 6 ($216k at risk); Monte Carlo pause share 75% -> 80%. Monte Carlo already shows A3 P50 m120 -$226k with kill rule.
proposed_change: Report kill-rule outcomes at the median and lead with the Monte Carlo pause share; avoid base values equal to thresholds.

challenge: Cash engine applies contingency only to development, one-time and pre-revenue run; the first-invoice model applies it to the full subtotal incl. live run. The lean live run ($465k base, unpriced assumptions AB010-AB017) gets no contingency.
evidence: Re-run with contingency on run: A3 peak $1.24M -> $1.44M, payback 62 -> 66; key figure cash to self-sufficiency corrected $222k/$1.24M/$16.97M -> $227k/$1.44M/$22.51M; H peak $4.97M -> $6.01M.
proposed_change: Use one contingency base across models 1 and 8 or show a run-contingency reserve line.

challenge: At the kill month all costs and revenue stop instantly; no wind-down (transition assistance, hosting through notice, cyber/E&O tail, SOC bridge letter, counsel).
evidence: Code inspection: active=false and live=0 after killAt; no termination cost term exists.
proposed_change: Add a wind-down cost at the kill month whenever a customer has signed.

challenge: All cash figures are pre-tax: no income tax after loss carry-forward, no sales/use tax on SaaS, no payroll tax on founder draw.
evidence: No tax term in Cashflow.fs or Capital.fs; A3 m120 $11.69M is labelled cash.
proposed_change: Label pre-tax or add a simple tax line.

challenge: AB's working-capital line included incident retention; the correction replaced it with the arrears receivable only, so no reserve remains for insurance deductibles, SLA credits or indemnities.
evidence: P3-ASM-AB023 basis text 'arrears billing, collection lag, incident retention'; Capital.toStream comment.
proposed_change: Restore a retention reserve as a one-time line at first go-live.

challenge: Arrears 1-4 months assume Echelon invoices the sponsor; under partner-first the partner bills and remits (quarterly, holdbacks) and the first sponsor is >25% of revenue for years; no bad-debt or concentration reserve.
evidence: Phase II 12 s4 concentration; no partner-remittance or credit term in model.
proposed_change: Separate partner-remittance lag range (3-6 months) and a concentration reserve until three customers are live.

challenge: Customer-funded variant treats implementation fees and advance billing as cost recovery/early cash; under ASC 606 non-distinct implementation fees are deferred revenue and pre-go-live billing is a refund liability if the pilot fails or is paused.
evidence: applyFunding sets ImplRecovery and negative arrears; no deferred revenue or refund term.
proposed_change: Keep the cash effect but add deferred-revenue and refund notes before calling it the cheapest lever.

challenge: Owner-facing headline is from S3, which does not exist; from today (S2, sequence A) base peak is $1.94M, payback 77, and the kill rule pauses at 24 after $1.14M. Paybacks are undiscounted.
evidence: sequences-cases A base; key-figures.
proposed_change: Lead with S2 figures and add discounted payback at the package's 10% rate.

challenge: variable_share is applied to vendor revenue after partner share, so serving cost falls when the partner share rises (partner-funded uplift). Model error.
evidence: Re-run applying it to gross revenue: partner-funded m120 A3 $9.87M -> $9.33M, A $7.16M -> $6.71M.
proposed_change: Apply variable_share to gross revenue (or convert to per-account cost).

challenge: The only paying sequence (A3) rests on Phase II ER-7 revenue ($300k net/customer) 'reused unchanged; untested' and already challenged in Phase II (CHL-081, CHL-082); the package's own FGJ sponsor price is $60k gross with 25% share.
evidence: Re-run A/A3 at FGJ terms ($25/60/150k, 15/25/40% share, per-account variable): A3 base peak $4.31M, m120 -$4.31M, no payback; uninterrupted MC no-payback 98% (vs 5%). Bisection: cash payback needs ~$110-120k net/customer-year; $150k pays back m96 (19 s5 says 'no payback', cash in fact pays back) but fully loaded -$534k.
proposed_change: Present the ranking at both revenue sets; make headline figures conditional on P3-GAP-MOD003 being closed; correct 19 s5 wording.

challenge: At $300k net a customer is ~5,300 accounts; the FY2024 panel has 25 sponsors that large (15 national, 5 processors, 3 religious, 2 single-issue, 0 community foundations) and 35 at the ~2,000-account payback threshold (2 CFs). A3 base needs ~30 signings in 10 years. The paying route is displacement of the least-mobile base.
evidence: Reviewer count on data/mission-2026-11-14/daf-long-tail-sponsors-fy2021-2024.csv (1,514 sponsors with accounts); sequences-horizons A3 m120 18.2 live; Phase II CHL-082.
proposed_change: Add a population check (non-captive sponsors per account band vs cumulative signings) and label A/A3 displacement sequences.

challenge: Not venture-scale: A3 uninterrupted MC P50 m120 $8.9M (P10 $1.3M, P90 $21.1M); with kill rule P50 -$226k. Licensing ceiling ~1.78M accounts x $81 = ~$144M/yr even if every account licensed. Externally funded variant prices equity as a 30% rate, ignoring dilution, control and investor appetite; no exit analysis.
evidence: monte-carlo table; Phase II CHL-083 account count, CHL-081, CHL-087; CLM-025 acquirers buy rather than license.
proposed_change: Replace 'externally funded' with owner capital, revenue-based debt and partner funding; add a strategic-sale scenario; state the outcome class (niche licensing business).

challenge: Response model converts ER-7 revenue into 15,873 new accounts a year and holds the lean cost base at base in all cases, producing 0.4-0.9 years to break-even; resilience claim inherits AB030.
evidence: Reviewer arithmetic at FGJ $60k/$81 (740 accts/sponsor, 3/yr, 8% churn): no-response break-even ~4.6 years; aggressive response (half wins) ~36 years.
proposed_change: State P3-CLM-MOD013 as conditional on AB030; add an FGJ-price variant to model 7.

challenge: Report 07 rates the largest advantage ordinary/low persistence and 13 models price cuts, but the sequence model holds price flat for ten years with 8% churn.
evidence: sequence-values.csv has no price-erosion field; 13 RS-1/RS-2 price cuts not fed to model 8.
proposed_change: Feed RS-1/RS-2 price paths into model 8 as variants.

challenge: Channel control treated as a tail: A3 has no partner churn/termination hazard although dependency is a channel partner; partner acquisition at m36 plus aggressive incumbent leaves A3 at -$1.34M.
evidence: extremes table; Phase II CHL-084; P3-ASM-FGJ016 partner termination 5-25%.
proposed_change: Carry partner termination as a base-case hazard in A, A3 and H.

target: Founder-months 120 in every platform sequence; Phase II CHL-015, CHL-088
challenge: Key-person risk: no hire in any sequence; one person carries sales, partner management, implementation, compliance ownership and product; TPRM vendor-viability review will see it.
evidence: sequences-cases founder-months column.
proposed_change: Add a staffing trigger and a key-person mitigation.

challenge: All-inputs-at-once corners (A3 +$88M / -$17M) are uninformative; the kill-rule Monte Carlo is the decision distribution.
evidence: monte-carlo table vs sequences-cases.
proposed_change: Lead with kill-rule Monte Carlo percentiles.

challenge: No licensing addressable market by sponsor size band (accounts, dollars, non-captive sponsors above the payback threshold) is stated anywhere in Phase III.
evidence: Data exist in the repository (SRC-013 panel).
proposed_change: Add a $0 desk calculation before ranking sequences.

challenge: 'Outside investment not necessary if the owner can fund the peak' is circular; from today (A) the peak is $1.94M and the base is paused at 24 after $1.14M.
evidence: sequences-cases A base; key-figures.
proposed_change: State cash required from today and founder personal runway per sequence; withdraw the claim until P3-GAP-MOD001 is answered.

target: sequence-values founder_fte 1, founder_cash_pre 0, founder_cash_live 60000; Phase II CHL-089
challenge: Hidden founder labour: one unpaid-then-$60k founder at a constant 1.0 FTE serves 18 enterprise sponsors (~95k accounts) by m120 as seller, implementer, second-line support, eligibility owner and SOC 2 control owner; flat run regardless of customers persists from Phase II.
evidence: sequences-horizons A3 m120 18.2 live; re-run with $30k/customer-year service: A3 peak $1.24M -> $1.34M, payback 62 -> 67.
proposed_change: Add a capacity constraint or hiring trigger; show months of unpaid founder work before first draw.

challenge: Remaining build ($600k cash vs $1.94M market) relies on unledgered agent productivity; MOD022's 0.31 ratio is derived from AB's own figure (circular); calling M-07 moot removes the only measurement.
evidence: Assumption basis texts; no spend ledger exists.
proposed_change: Start a $0 hours and cash ledger now and report actual against AB002 monthly.

challenge: Ramen profitability is ~47 months from today (A base) on a $60k draw with a named partner by month 6; forgone salary ~$0.9M; no comparison with the founder's real alternative (consulting/other Echelon revenue).
evidence: sequences-ranking A sustainable from 47; A3 38 from S3.
proposed_change: Add a do-nothing/consult baseline at $0 DAF cash.

challenge: Only the 04 validation ladder ($1-25k) is bootstrappable; the entry path spends on S3 first, off the kill-rule clock.
evidence: 16 s6; kill-sensitivity.
proposed_change: Make named partner plus non-binding price expression (V-6 plus V-2) a precondition for further DAF-specific build.

target: P3-ASM-AB020 / impl_later $10-80k; Phase II CHL-073, CHL-077
challenge: Later-customer implementation at $30k base for ~5,000-account full-history migrations is under-costed or is hidden founder labour.
evidence: Phase II 584-934 sponsor hours per 10k-fund conversion; multiple rehearsals.
proposed_change: Price implementation from the Transitus rehearsal plan and charge it.

challenge: Side bets are modelled as FTE fractions but never delay the A/H first signing month, so diversion looks free.
evidence: Sequences.fs has no coupling between founder allocation and first_signing_month.
proposed_change: Model diversion as signing delay or drop side bets until a pilot is live.

challenge: No account-management or service cost per live customer beyond the revenue-share variable cost.
evidence: Re-run +$30k/customer-year: A3 peak $1.34M, payback 67.
proposed_change: Add a per-customer service line.

challenge: F gross margin is -18% (support $2,360 vs revenue $2,000) yet report 09 recommends self-serve commercial licences.
evidence: sequences-horizons F gross margin -18%; P3-ASM-FGJ015.
proposed_change: Publish terms with no support offer, or price at $5k or more.

target: events-by-party ($30 platform + $3 AI per acct-yr); P3-ASM-MOD003 ($12.15); P3-ASM-AB010..AB017; P3-GAP-MOD004
challenge: Model inconsistency: model 2 says automated work reappears as platform cost of ~$33/account-year, but neither the lean run nor A/A3 variable cost ($12.15) carries it.
evidence: Re-run A3 at ~$33/acct (variable share 0.58): peak $1.82M, payback 96, economic m120 -$0.34M, uninterrupted MC no-payback 33% (vs 5%).
proposed_change: Carry the event model's platform residual into model 8; mark P3-GAP-MOD004 blocking.

challenge: Capital minimization is an unmeasured AI-productivity bet (dev at 31% of market; maintenance $120k vs 1-2 engineers $0.22-0.47M).
evidence: Re-run maintenance +$230k/yr: A3 peak $1.59M, payback 70. Stacked with event-consistent platform cost and run contingency: A3 base no payback (m120 -$1.03M, economic -$5.06M, peak $3.24M); uninterrupted MC no-payback 67%, with ER-7 revenue unchanged.
proposed_change: Label AI-dependent cost lines as a hypothesis with a measurement plan; show the stacked variant.

challenge: Event minutes are Phase II assumptions; automated minutes are removed entirely with an unmeasured 10-50% charge-back; no exception-tail measurement (adjacent industries keep 5-15%).
evidence: 10 s11 concedes nothing is measured except the Schedule I replay.
proposed_change: Report event savings conditional on V-7/pilot measurement; do not feed price floors until measured.

challenge: Savings are process redesign and deterministic automation that incumbents already claim, not AI; benchmark is a 'conventional' administrator, not a well-automated incumbent (gap $11-71).
evidence: 07 s4; 13 s4; Ren VENDOR-CLAIM >50% instant approvals.
proposed_change: Report savings versus best-automated incumbent and split by redesign / deterministic automation / AI.

challenge: Ten-year real-terms model with no wage or price escalation hides a Baumol margin squeeze: residual mandatory labour, counsel, insurance and audit rise faster than per-account licence prices, which face compression.
evidence: No escalation terms in model; 13 price-cut scenarios.
proposed_change: Add a variant escalating residual labour and assurance 2-3 points above licence price.

challenge: Registry run is computed at one sponsor and added as a constant for the whole horizon although union-charity scaling grows with sponsors. Model error.
evidence: registry-marginal: ~$26k/sponsor average at 10 sponsors (~$260k total) vs $87k addable.
proposed_change: Make RegistryRunAnnual a function of live sponsors.

challenge: Possible double count in the economic view: dev_econ is the market value of the build while the founder is also charged at 1 FTE market during the same months.
evidence: AB002 basis 'founder time excluded (shown in economic)'; overstatement up to ~$111k (A3) / ~$333k (A).
proposed_change: State whether founder build hours are inside dev_econ; net them out if so.

challenge: Licensing moves ~53 residual minutes to the sponsor at x1.4; willingness to pay must be tested against the sponsor's all-in cost (licence plus ~$67/acct staffed residual), not the licence price alone.
evidence: events-by-party staffed residual $67.
proposed_change: Add the all-in comparison to the V-2 script.

challenge: Validation is not independent (same model family authored and reviewed); almost all productivity inputs are ASSUMPTION/INFERENCE.
evidence: 02 header statement.
proposed_change: Have one human practitioner check maintenance FTE, implementation hours per 1,000 accounts and exception rate.

challenge: A3 is a state of A, not a choice; ranking it first beside S2-start sequences is apples-to-oranges, and completing S3 'inside existing operations' moves ~$0.8M of spend off the kill-rule clock (A flips from paused to pass when the cost-center month moves to 12+), inverting DEC-008.
evidence: kill-sensitivity A rows; sequences-cases A base peak $1.94M vs paused $1.14M.
proposed_change: Show A3 only as 'A conditional on S3' with S2->S3 cost attached; decide P3-DEC-MOD001 with this trade stated.

target: DEC-001; 05; 06; sequences E/G/H vs A/A3; 16 s6 step 5
challenge: Approved positioning (partner-first, small/mid and new programmes) never pays back; the paying positioning (ER-7-scale sponsors) is displacement of the least-switching segment. 16 s6 step 5 silently swaps positioning.
evidence: sequences-ranking; Phase II CHL-082; SRC-013 panel counts (P3-CHL-REV2012).
proposed_change: Put an explicit positioning choice to the owner: niche licensing to mid/large sponsors via a partner that has them, or greenfield enablement priced to carry a licensor.

challenge: Sequencing: building S3 before a named partner risks building the wrong product for the partner's integration, tenancy and data-rights needs.
evidence: Re-run threshold: A3 cash payback needs ~$110-120k net per customer (~2,000 accounts).
proposed_change: Gate further DAF-specific build on a named partner, a price expression at or above that level and one candidate sponsor of at least 2,000 accounts.

challenge: Fragmentation across sequences, entities, components, adjacent industries and services; B, C, D, F, G each fail standalone.
evidence: sequences-ranking.
proposed_change: Publish an explicit do-not-build list; keep charity intelligence and Transitus as internal Unbound capabilities.

challenge: Component commercialization recommended despite F's -18% gross margin and founder-time support cost.
evidence: sequences-horizons F.
proposed_change: Publish terms only; remove F from the ranking.

challenge: Ranking by m120 cumulative cash puts F third for losing least; no $0 do-nothing baseline; under the kill rule no sequence has a positive median (A3 P50 -$226k).
evidence: sequences-ranking; monte-carlo applied rows.
proposed_change: Add a do-nothing row and rank on kill-rule Monte Carlo percentiles.

challenge: Any dedicated stream's go-live counts as the DAF pilot, so B passes on a fraction of an $8k/yr API customer and then burns $5.78M.
evidence: sequences-cases B base 'passes'; 14 s2 acknowledges.
proposed_change: Require the pilot to be an Unbound (E2) sponsor stream.

challenge: The greenfield (3,056 edu/health institutions) is blocked by demand, free alternatives and regulatory responsibility, 'not technology'; only a hosted programme service addresses it, and E does not carry a licensor.
evidence: 05 answer items 2-5; sequences-ranking E.
proposed_change: Reframe 05's market as a service-partner market, not evidence of licence demand.

challenge: S7 shared-infrastructure state ($583k cash to first invoice) appears in owner tables although no second revenue-bearing product exists.
evidence: 15 answer item 1; P3-CLM-MOD009.
proposed_change: Mark S7 hypothetical or remove from owner-facing tables.
